defense_opportunities: Two-tier system also benefits defense — DWAI is a lesser charge with lighter penalties, providing negotiation room when BAC is borderline.

common_defenses: Rising blood alcohol defense — BAC at time of driving was below the legal limit but rose during absorption phase before testing.
Medical conditions (GERD, diabetes, ketosis) producing falsely elevated breath test results.

prosecution_strengths: Per se BAC violation requires only proof BAC was .08% or higher within 2 hours of driving — no proof of impairment required.

defense_opportunities: Colorado's Diversion programs in some judicial districts allow first offenders to complete alcohol treatment in lieu of conviction.
Margin of error in breath testing instruments can create reasonable doubt for borderline BAC results near .08%.
Challenge the calibration and certification records of the Intoxilyzer 9000 used by Colorado law enforcement.
common_defenses: Lack of probable cause for the traffic stop or DUI arrest — Fourth Amendment challenge to suppress all derivative evidence.
Rising blood alcohol — BAC was below .08% at time of driving, supported by toxicology expert testimony.
Improper administration of breath test or failure to follow CDPHE-approved procedures.
Mouth alcohol contamination from belching, GERD, or recent consumption producing falsely elevated breath reading.

prosecution_strengths: Mandatory minimums increase with each conviction — second offense requires 10 days jail; third offense requires 60 days; fourth+ requires felony charge with prison.

Negotiate to DWAI plea to break the enhancement chain and reduce mandatory consequences.

prosecution_strengths: Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) protocol is admissible in Colorado courts to establish drug impairment without per se limits.
